epicOrder.description: Authoritative implementation sequence for epics with open stories. Claude Code works the first epic in 'sequence' that has stories not yet Passed/Dropped/Deferred, unless the handoff prompt says otherwise. Maintained only via tdd-spec-session — implementation sessions never reorder this. NOTE: an epic whose stories have all Passed is REMOVED from this sequence (its rows live in project-tracker-archive.json), so 'first epic in sequence' stays meaningful — Epic MFTF-23 was removed 2026-08-17 for exactly this reason, having been left here after US-MFTF-23.1 passed and archived.

sequence.rationale: Listings must exist before the storefront has anything to show.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-13: Referenced Apparel Listings (Teemill Product Ref)
sequence.rationale: Second apparel sourcing mode (Teemill product ref). US-MFTF-13.1 additively extends the MFTF-5.1 schema and must land before MFTF-6 so browse/detail can render both designed and referenced listings from one normalized read-shape.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-6: Apparel Product Page & Browse
sequence.rationale: Buyers need browse and product pages, rendering BOTH sourcing modes (designed + referenced) via the normalized read-shape; the cart button ships stubbed here per US-MFTF-6.2. Depends on MFTF-13 schema.
DB-backed guest-capable cart; wires the MFTF-6.2 button and reworks print ordering (US-15.4) into add-to-cart.
Replaces Epic MFTF-7. Multi-line-item Stripe checkout, per-provider order splitting and fan-out. US-MFTF-12.5/12.6 close out as the webhook epic (MFTF-14) supplies live status detection.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-14: Provider Webhooks, Status Mapping & Lifecycle Emails
sequence.rationale: Makes provider status flow back automatically (Prodigi webhooks; Teemill webhook-or-polling fork) and sends the three buyer lifecycle emails (PRINTING/SHIPPED/DELIVERED). Retires the polling TODO in US-MFTF-12.6 and is the live-confirmation those two pending stories need.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-15: Seller Fulfillment for Originals
sequence.rationale: Hybrid split: physical-original fulfillment moves admin→seller (seller-scoped queue); admin retains a dropship-exception/retry queue re-homed from US-14.5. Dropship fulfillment stays fully automated. Depends on MFTF-14 for status/email plumbing.

Two small Passed-story revisions: remove Teemill from the designed-mode provider picker (enum retained, UI-blocked); default the first colour on the apparel detail page (size stays un-pre-selected). Independent of fulfillment; can land alongside MFTF-14/15.

Material-standard gate cleared 2026-07-11 (qualifying styles confirmed). Currently being implemented. Three-phase shape: US-MFTF-17.1 API discovery spike resolves DESIGNED vs REFERENCED sourcing mode (unlike Teemill, not obvious up front); US-MFTF-17.2 implements the FulfillmentProvider subclass behind that finding; US-MFTF-17.3 is a founder-executed live-order confirmation gating Passed status. Depends on MFTF-12.1 (abstract base, Passed) and MFTF-14.2 (status mapping).

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-PF: Print Framing, Canvas Wrap & Seller Mockups
sequence.rationale: Print fidelity: seller-controlled per-aspect framing crop (canvas+paper) + canvas wrap (seller-fixed, MirrorWrap default, ImageWrap UI-blocked) + seller-uploaded per-size buyer mockups. Hard gate blocks ACTIVE until every offered aspect is framed AND every offered size has a mockup; strict archive-on-deploy for non-compliant live listings. Touches Passed US-15.2/15.4/15.6/15.7 and replaces the hardcoded fillPrintArea/no-wrap path in prodigi.ts. Independent of the fulfillment loop; slotted after MFTF-16 around the print work. Founder-ratified 2026-06-21.

Founder decision 2026-06-17, ratified in the 2026-06-18 spec session: sequenced after the fulfillment loop (MFTF-14/15) and before MFTF-10. MFTF-12 cart checkout shipped with Stripe automatic_tax disabled (STRIPE_TAX_ENABLED, default false) because Stripe Tax needs per-price tax_behavior + product tax categories + registration. Epic 5 wires that up and re-enables automatic_tax before launch.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-19: Storefront Polish & Pricing Visibility
sequence.rationale: Quality-of-life storefront polish + Teemill US-pricing visibility. Independent of the launch-critical path; 19.1 revises the Passed MFTF-6.2 carousel, 19.5/19.6 add founder curation tooling. Sequenced after core fulfillment, before the Pre-Launch Checklist.
Open chores (CHORE-1 Vercel Pro/auction crons, CHORE-2 DNS, CHORE-4 live credentials, CHORE-16 commit-hash backfill) slot in around launch as needed.

Public About page (vision/goals, Who We Are founder bios, material-standard commitment). Scoped 2026-07-11 as admin-editable content (small CMS), not static copy — bios/photos reuse the existing Blob image pipeline. Independent of fulfillment; sequenced after MFTF-19 polish and before the Pre-Launch Checklist since a public site should have this before go-live.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-21: Contact Page & Feedback Form
sequence.rationale: Public Contact page with feedback form emailing ThePeople@MerchForTheFuture via MailerSend, plus honeypot spam protection and per-IP rate limiting. Scoped 2026-07-11 alongside MFTF-20 (same pre-launch public-pages motivation); no schema dependency between the two epics.

sequence.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
sequence.rationale: Merchandising layer over the apparel catalog: Men's/Women's/Whatevs categories, admin-managed collections (seeded New + Our Favorites), a page per category and collection, a path-aware product breadcrumb, and an Apparel nav dropdown (desktop + mobile). Scoped 2026-08-17. Sequenced BEFORE MFTF-22 deliberately: US-MFTF-24.6 supersedes US-MFTF-22.3's fixed Home-Shop-Product BreadcrumbList, and MFTF-24 adds four new public routes that MFTF-22's sitemap and per-page metadata must cover — doing SEO first would mean writing it twice. Independent of the fulfillment critical path; depends only on MFTF-5/MFTF-13 (listings) and MFTF-6.1 (the browse projection it reuses).

Technical SEO foundation: sitemap.xml, robots.txt, complete per-page metadata (title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter), and Product/Organization/Breadcrumb JSON-LD structured data. Scoped 2026-07-11. Sequenced after MFTF-20/MFTF-21 (About/Contact must exist to be included in the sitemap and get metadata), after MFTF-24 (its category/collection routes need sitemap + metadata coverage, and US-MFTF-24.6 revises the US-MFTF-22.3 breadcrumb), and before MFTF-10, since the new US-MFTF-10.9 (Search Console verification) depends on the sitemap this epic produces.

Moved to end of sequence 2026-07-11 (after Infrastructure) per founder decision: go-live is the final gate and should follow all other work including open infrastructure chores (Vercel Pro, DNS, live credentials), not precede them. Production readiness; largely human tasks (business registration, live keys, samples).

stories.title: Post-Payment Fulfillment Fan-Out
stories.notes: On PAID, the webhook CART branch calls dispatchOrderFulfillment(orderId) which dispatches each FulfillmentOrder through provider.fulfill() (the 12.1 template). Implemented the fulfill() steps: Prodigi createProviderOrder (multi-item POST /orders; single-step, default no-op confirm); Teemill two-step createProviderOrder (POST /orders) + confirmProviderOrder (POST /orders/{id}/confirm with the quoted shippingMethodId — // UNVERIFIED 'standard', Open Q#7). Per-shipment FAILURE ISOLATION: any error sets that FulfillmentOrder FAILED + notes and does not throw, so siblings proceed. IDEMPOTENT per FulfillmentOrder: skipped once providerOrderId is set (no duplicate provider orders on webhook replay). Admin retry: retryFulfillmentAction (admin-only) + a 'Failed shipments' section with a Retry button on /admin/fulfillment (US-14.5 page). Job items resolve referenced variantRef from the cached ReferencedVariant by colour+size, designed apparel to providerSkuBase, prints to prodigiSku + printSourceImageUrl. Legacy single-item PRINT webhook path left as-is (cart prints now route through the abstraction). MSW: Teemill POST /orders/:id/confirm + GET /orders/:ref added globally. MFTF-3 provider tests re-run green. DOWNGRADED to 'Tests Passing — pending live confirmation' (2026-06-17, founder): actually SUBMITTING an order — Teemill POST /orders → /confirm — charges real money, so the founder is intentionally not running it live yet; live order placement (incl. the designed→Prodigi order with the design asset, fanout buildJobItems) is therefore unverified against the real APIs. Logic is fully green vs MSW; flip to Passed after a real proofing order confirms the two-step confirm + the Prodigi designed order succeed. PLAN (founder, 2026-06-17): live confirmation is intentionally deferred — a live Teemill order costs real money, so the founders will combine it with their FIRST design-proof order (the proof print doubles as the live integration test). Until that order is placed and observed, 12.5 stays at this status. Everything is green vs MSW and the cart→checkout→payment path is live-verified in Stripe test mode.

stories.title: Buyer Order View with Per-Shipment Status
stories.notes: Implemented + green against MSW (8 tests incl. a jsdom component test). getOrderShipmentsView groups a cart order's items into 'Shipment N of M' with per-shipment status + tracking and NEVER exposes provider names; OrderShipments component renders it on the confirmation page and the Epic 22 order detail page (CART branch). aggregateOrderStatus → order history shows 'Processing' until all shipments SHIPPED then 'Shipped' (getBuyerOrders CART branch). checkFulfillmentStatus() on the provider abstraction: Prodigi reads shipments[].tracking over its order GET (same data its webhook carries); Teemill polls GET /orders/{orderRef}. checkAndSyncShipments (daily cron /api/cron/teemill-shipments, schedule 0 6 * * *, Hobby-compatible, CRON_SECRET) marks dispatched shipments SHIPPED + tracking/carrier and sends a per-shipment MailerSend email (sendShipmentShippedEmail — only that shipment's items; identical path for poll vs webhook); idempotent (only CONFIRMED+providerOrderId are polled). HELD at non-Passed (Option B, founder decision): Open Q#2 — Teemill webhook support unconfirmed, so shipment status is polling with a '// TODO: replace Teemill polling with webhook once payload shape is confirmed live' marker and the tracking field paths / dispatched-status value marked // UNVERIFIED; needs a live proofing order before Passed. No live API calls in tests (MSW only). PLAN (founder, 2026-06-17): same as 12.5 — shipment-status/polling + the per-shipment SHIPPED email can only be observed after a real order exists, so this is deferred to the founders' first Teemill design-proof order (a live order costs money, so it doubles as a proof print). Buyer order views + aggregate status are verifiable in test mode today; the SHIPPED transition + tracking + email await that first live order.

stories.title: Printify Provider Integration
stories.notes: DESIGNED-mode Printify integration per the US-MFTF-17.1 spike (docs/printify-api-notes.md). Tests written first and confirmed RED before implementation: __tests__/mftf-17-printify/US-MFTF-17.2-printify-provider.test.ts (provider contract, two-step create→send-to-production, USD cents→dollars quote, status/webhook mapping, HMAC signature, @ts-expect-error incomplete-subclass), US-MFTF-17.2-printify-designed-catalog.test.ts (curated (blueprint,print_provider) sync of colours/sizes/combo→variantId map + admin create/update PRINTIFY validation), US-MFTF-17.2-printify-fanout-split.test.ts (multi-provider split, order-line correctness, failure isolation, buyer-opacity). All 25 green vs MSW; the 40-file fulfillment/checkout/catalog regression set (336 tests) stays green. Implementation: PrintifyFulfillmentProvider (src/lib/fulfillment/providers/printify.ts) + printify/client.ts; getProviderByKey 'printify'; ProductTypePrintifyVariant combo table + printifyBlueprintId/printifyPrintProviderId on ProductType (providerSkuBase made nullable); sync-printify.ts; fanout.ts + revalidate.ts Printify branches; api/webhooks/printify/route.ts (HMAC-SHA256, marked // UNVERIFIED header, polling is primary); admin ProductTypeForm + product-catalog actions; MSW printifyHandlers; env vars in .env.local.example + runbook. HELD at 'Tests Passing — pending live confirmation' (not Passed): status vocabulary, create-order response, send-to-production requirement, and webhook signature header are // UNVERIFIED with no Printify sandbox — they resolve at US-MFTF-17.3 (founder live order), which gates Passed. FOLLOW-UP (2026-08-15): catalog sync corrected to pass ?show-out-of-stock=1 — the default variants.json hides out-of-stock variants (blueprint 1580/provider 99: 4 default vs 16 full), so without it the cached catalog was incomplete/volatile (docs/printify-api-notes.md stock-semantics corrected; scripts/printify-blueprint-lookup.ts added to resolve a product URL → blueprint/provider/variant ids). Live per-variant orderability (product-page grey-out + checkout re-check) is scoped as US-MFTF-17.4. FIX (2026-08-15): buyer checkout hit 'Printify shipping quote (POST /orders/shipping.json) failed (404)' because PRINTIFY_SHOP_ID was unset in .env.local, so shop-scoped calls built a malformed /shops//orders/... path. The client now resolves the shop id (resolvePrintifyShopId): PRINTIFY_SHOP_ID if set, else GET /shops.json once (cached), throwing a clear error if the account has no shop; shopPath is now async. Live-verified: shop 28204676 resolved, shipping calc → 200 {standard:475}. Setting PRINTIFY_SHOP_ID=28204676 still avoids the extra call. FIX #2 (2026-08-15): with the shop id resolved, order-create then 400'd (code 8150 'src/x/y/scale/angle required') — our print_areas used the PRODUCT-creation shape. The ORDER endpoint wants print_areas as an OBJECT keyed by position with the design URL: print_areas: { front: <url> } (Printify auto-centres). Fixed in createProviderOrder (dropped the /uploads step; positioned {src,x,y,scale,angle} form deferred to the 17.7 placement tool). docs/printify-api-notes.md updated. Still // UNVERIFIED: src=URL-vs-upload-id + the create RESPONSE shape — confirmed only by an order that reaches production (US-MFTF-17.3).

stories.title: Order-Time Placement Wiring
stories.notes: Tests Passing — pending live confirmation (2026-08-17, TDD, tests RED before impl). The ~5-line order-time wiring anticipated in the original emerging-need note. toQuoteItem (src/lib/checkout/fanout.ts) reads the listing's saved ApparelListingPrintifyPlacement (added to foInclude) and attaches it to the ShippingQuoteItem as a new optional placement:{x,y,scale,angle} field; omitted when no row. PrintifyFulfillmentProvider.createProviderOrder emits the POSITIONED print_areas form { [pos]: [{ src, x, y, scale, angle }] } when item.placement is present, and the existing simple URL form { [pos]: '<url>' } when absent — zero regression risk for listings that never used the tool. No other provider touched; quoteShipping unaffected; buyer-opacity unaffected (placement is a seller-side production detail). Tests: __tests__/mftf-17-printify/US-MFTF-17.9-printify-positioned-order.test.ts (4: provider positioned-vs-simple + a regression pin on the simple form protecting every already-live listing; fan-out end-to-end with/without a saved placement row). 4 green; broad fulfillment/checkout regression (39 files / 252 tests incl. mftf-3/12/14/15/17) green. HELD at pending-live-confirmation (NOT Passed), per the epic convention: whether the positioned form (and src=URL) reaches Printify PRODUCTION correctly is // UNVERIFIED without a live order — confirm by piggybacking on US-MFTF-17.3, or a dedicated live check if 17.3 has closed by the time this ships. Depends on US-MFTF-17.8. NOTE (2026-08-17): a post-merge placement-tool UI polish (60% default design size, blank-not-lifestyle backdrop, edit-page colour swatches) explicitly PRESERVED this story's invariant -- defaultPlacement() stays scale 1 so a listing with NO saved row still emits the simple (auto-centre) form; only the tool's starting DISPLAY changed. stories.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
stories.title: Category & Collection Schema
stories.notes: Category (kind MANUAL|ALL_APPAREL) + ApparelListingCategory many-to-many; Collection (kind MANUAL|AUTO_NEW) + CollectionListing with a nullable PIN|EXCLUDE override. Seeds Men's/Women's/Whatevs and New/Our Favorites. Whatevs is ALL_APPAREL (derived, never join rows); New is AUTO_NEW (recency window ∪ pins − excludes) behind one shared membership resolver so no page reimplements it. ALSO defines hasDurableGrouping(listingId) — true iff the listing has a MANUAL category or MANUAL collection membership, deliberately NOT counting Whatevs (everything is in it) or New (membership decays) — the single definition consumed by the US-MFTF-24.5 activation gate and the US-MFTF-24.3 last-grouping warning. Blocks every other story in the epic.

stories.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
stories.title: Admin Collection Management
stories.notes: /admin/collections CRUD + membership curation + reordering, admin-guarded (rejects seller and buyer, not just anonymous). The AUTO_NEW collection surfaces pin/exclude rather than add/remove and visibly distinguishes the three states. Seeded New and Our Favorites cannot be deleted (nav + breadcrumb default trail depend on them) but can be renamed/reordered/deactivated. LAST-GROUPING WARNING: deleting/deactivating a collection or removing a listing from one warns (advisory, non-blocking) when the action would leave ACTIVE listings with no durable grouping — this closes the one gap the US-MFTF-24.5 publish-time gate can't cover, since that gate stops a listing going live ungrouped but not a live listing losing its last grouping afterwards. Depends on US-MFTF-24.1.

stories.notes: /shop/collections/[slug] + a /shop/collections index. MANUAL collections order by curated sortOrder; AUTO_NEW orders newest-first with pins first. One visibility rule for inactive collections applied to the index, the nav dropdown, and the page (404) — asserted together in one test so the three can't drift. Depends on US-MFTF-24.1 (and 24.3 for anything to curate).

stories.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
stories.title: Seller Category Assignment & Activation Gate
stories.notes: Multi-select for the MANUAL categories on both the designed (MFTF-5.3/5.4) and referenced (MFTF-13.3/13.4) listing forms — categorization must not branch on sourcingMode. Whatevs is never offered (it's automatic) and is rejected if injected into the payload directly. ACTIVATION GATE (founder-ratified 2026-08-17, revising an earlier optional-membership pass): a listing cannot be created as or transitioned to ACTIVE unless hasDurableGrouping is true; drafts save freely, matching the MFTF-PF publish-gate precedent. Enforced server-side in the action, not only by a disabled button. NOTE the gate is deliberately NOT 'is in New' — the founder's first formulation — because New is recency-derived, so every listing is in it at publish (the check could never fail) and drops out ~a window later (exactly when the listing becomes unreachable); a test pins the Whatevs+New-only case as rejected so this can't regress. Existing ACTIVE listings are logged, NOT auto-archived — a deliberate divergence from MFTF-PF's strict archive-on-deploy, since an uncategorized listing is a discoverability gap rather than a defective product. Depends on US-MFTF-24.1.

stories.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
stories.title: Path-Aware Breadcrumb on the Product Page
stories.notes: REVISES US-MFTF-22.3 (still Not Started). Navigation context travels as a ?from=category:<slug>|collection:<slug> query param — URL-carried so it survives refresh, is server-rendered, and is unit-testable. Labels are ALWAYS resolved by DB lookup, never echoed from the param; an unknown, inactive, or non-member context falls back to the default trail so the breadcrumb never asserts a false path. Default trail (founder-specified): Home → Whatevs → first collection by Collection.sortOrder (ties by slug) → listing title. Canonical URL ignores ?from= (US-MFTF-22.2's no-query-string-drift rule) and the BreadcrumbList JSON-LD always emits the DEFAULT trail, never the visitor-specific one. Pure src/lib/apparel/breadcrumb.ts module mirrors the crop-geometry/placement-geometry precedent. Depends on US-MFTF-24.1/24.2/24.4.

stories.epic: Epic MFTF-24: Apparel Categories, Collections & Navigation
stories.title: Apparel Navigation Dropdown (Desktop & Mobile)
stories.notes: Apparel dropdown in the primary nav: New, Men's, Women's, Whatevs, then remaining active collections (capped, with a 'See all collections' overflow link). Opens on hover AND keyboard focus — hover alone is keyboard-inaccessible — reusing the Epic 23 NavDropdown interaction contract (Escape returns focus, outside-click, aria-expanded, role=menu) rather than a second pattern; includes a close-delay/bridge for the diagonal-pointer failure mode. The trigger is itself a link to /shop. Data-driven, so deactivating a collection removes it with no code change. MobileMenu gets a tap-to-expand equivalent (no hover on touch). Depends on US-MFTF-24.1/24.2/24.4.
